assumptions: This evaluation covers only version 4 as a planning-stage, fixed-fee diagnostic; it does not credit capabilities excluded from that version or any performance attributed to an earlier version.
The customer supplies contract-authorized exports for one retailer and one deduction class, while the service performs no portal impersonation, dispute submission, or legal determination.
Pricing, recoverable value, delivery hours, adviser economics, conversion, repeat demand, and template transferability remain hypotheses rather than established commercial facts.
The founder maintains complete separation from employer-confidential data, contacts, and processes and obtains independent conflict clearance before selling.
Specialist finance, security, or legal review can be contracted when required, but its cost and time must be included in contribution economics and cannot be replaced by AI automation.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: The pre-integration evidence-readiness audit targets a credible gap between structured invoices and the promotion, remittance, proof-of-performance, and outcome records needed to pursue deductions. Narrowing to one retailer and claim class makes the insight testable, but it is an inferred service gap inside a mature workflow rather than a demonstrated market misunderstanding.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: Retail deductions can tie up cash and consume finance labor, and incumbent products plus the vendor-reported mid-market case support the existence of the problem. The reviewed evidence does not establish the incidence, recoverable value, urgency, budget owner, or fixed-audit willingness to pay among the proposed Polish and CEE beachhead.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: A quoted fixed fee, prepaid scope, customer-created exports, and a capped case batch reduce capital exposure, open-ended labor, and recovery-attribution disputes. However, price, adviser share, acquisition cost, delivery and review hours, gross margin, payback, repeat volume, retention, owner earnings, and the founder-net-worth path are all unverified; the default model is a potentially bespoke one-off audit.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: The beachhead is operationally precise: a mid-sized Polish or CEE CPG supplier, one retailer, one high-value deduction class, a material unresolved batch, usable evidence, and an inadequate current workflow. That precision aids qualification but creates a highly conjunctive segment whose customer count and economic size are unknown and may be small.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: The no-integration diagnostic may serve accounts that cannot justify a full platform, but SAP, HighRadius, Vistex, Inmar, advisers, and internal finance teams already cover much of the underlying job. No exclusive channel, proprietary access, superior recovery rate, cost advantage, or underserved local segment has been demonstrated, so a dominant position is presently difficult to support.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: Successful audits could extend into prepaid recurring batch review, additional deduction classes and retailers, and adjacent CEE markets. Those adjacencies are logically close, but each adds permissions, retailer-specific maintenance, human review, and direct competition, and no evidence yet shows that one-off diagnostic demand converts into a scalable recurring product.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Permissioned retailer templates, completeness rules, and outcome labels could modestly improve triage and delivery over time. Their transferability and data rights are unknown, the starting service is reproducible by advisers or incumbents, GS1 and KSeF reduce normalization scarcity, and the concept has no established switching costs, exclusive relationships, or proprietary dataset.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: A bounded audit without live connectors offers lower commitment, faster experimentation, clearer scope, and potentially lower cost than a broad implementation. There is no comparative evidence that it delivers more incremental recovery, lower total handling cost, better evidence, or faster resolution than existing staff, advisers, or established systems, so the behavior-changing advantage remains hypothetical.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: Poland's KSeF transition can make standardized invoice exports easier and create a moment to reassess finance workflows. The same change commoditizes invoice extraction, while mature standards and current incumbent offerings show that the broader category is established rather than newly opened; timing is mixed rather than unusually favorable.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: An ERP or EDI adviser could supply trust, installed-account access, and a co-branded route that fits the founder's preference for lower-social-intensity selling. No adviser has committed, channel economics and lead flow are unknown, advisers may already solve the problem, and excluding employer-derived contacts leaves initial acquisition with no demonstrated repeatable path.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: The PLN 18,000 planning envelope, capped audit, absence of persistent connectors, and data-analysis work fit the founder's capital and technical profile better than a broad platform. Execution still depends on complete authorized evidence, finance-domain judgment, security and data-processing controls, adviser coordination, conflict clearance, and unmeasured delivery hours that may exceed a part-time operating model.

main_structural_strength: A sharply bounded, low-capital diagnostic can test the economically relevant gap before committing to integrations or recurring software, while producing an explicit go/no-go signal from real customer data.
primary_score_limiter: The business requires a narrow intersection of material unresolved deductions, complete authorized evidence, an inadequate incumbent workflow, budget, and adviser access, yet neither the size of that intersection nor repeatable profitable delivery has been shown.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: HighRadius documents nearly the full supplier-side capture, promotion-matching, evidence, dispute, and ERP workflow, while a Vistex case study reports meaningful deduction-processing improvement at a 200-plus-employee food producer; together they directly weaken the claim that the target job or mid-market customer is meaningfully underserved.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: At least three independently sourced Polish or CEE supplier datasets should show material recoverable deductions left unresolved by current staff or systems, followed by paid fixed-scope audits that establish accepted pricing, attributable cash or labor value, bounded delivery hours, positive contribution margin after expert review and adviser share, and repeat eligible volume; at least one adviser should commit to commercial terms and produce qualified introductions.
highest_value_structural_change: Make the diagnostic an adviser-embedded, standardized pre-implementation product only after one adviser commits to distribution and a paid customer validates a fixed export schema, delivery SLA, and contribution margin; then tie any recurring module to documented repeat case volume rather than positioning the one-off audit itself as the scalable business.
